$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 8 of N, 2026-11-23 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.lifecycleState.initial: A record has to begin somewhere; marking one state as the initial one makes every new row start there, so no caller can invent a starting status and the first transition always leaves a known place.
reasons.flowStep.checkpoint: A declared rule inside a flow can guard the work before it runs, to refuse bad input early, or after it, to catch the state the work produced; pre or post picks the moment, so one invariant check serves either side without two copies of the rule.
reasons.queryLookup.fn: A report line often needs a figure from related rows, such as how many open tickets a customer has or what they spent; the function picks count, sum, average, minimum or maximum, and a row with nothing to match gets 0 for count and sum and empty otherwise, so the report needs no hand-written join and total.
reasons.conversion.when: A data migration that turns old codes into new ones, such as 'A' into 'ACTIVE', needs a list of cases tried in order where the first match wins; the list keeps the mapping in the model, readable and reviewable, and not in a script run once and lost.
reasons.humanTask.fields: When a flow waits for a person, for example an approver who must give a reason, the person fills a small form; the fields name each input, and their values come back with the completed event so the flow continues with them, instead of the answer travelling through a side screen the flow knows nothing about.
reasons.pack:sequences: A pack that offers invoicing needs its own document-number counter; listing the counter in the pack brings it along on install, and its name is kept as written so documents numbered before and after an upgrade share one series.
reasons.root:concepts: An app is first of all the kinds of record it keeps; this list declares them, at least one, and every screen, flow and query refers back to a concept by name, so nothing can describe data the app does not hold.
reasons.panelWidget.span: On a dashboard a chart needs more room than a counter; the span is how many of the four grid columns a widget takes, so one number sets the proportions without custom styling.
reasons.httpConnectorOperation.query: Calling an outside service often needs query-string values, such as a page size or a filter; the map names them, and a value that renders empty drops its key, so an optional filter does not send a blank parameter the remote service would read as a real value.
reasons.queryLookup.on: To attach a figure from another concept to each row of a query, the lookup must say how the two match, for example the lookup's customer id against the query's customer id; the join keys state that pairing, so the platform does the join and the author writes no SQL.
reasons.enumOption.label: A choice value such as IN_PROGRESS is a code the system stores; the label is the text a person reads in forms and lists, one plain string or one per language, so the stored code never changes when the wording or the language does.
reasons.panelFieldBinding.ui: One field may need a different look on one panel than the concept's default gives it, such as a wide note area; presentation hints on the binding apply to that panel only, so the same data is shown differently without declaring a second field.
reasons.aggregateFunction.name: An aggregate query returns totals, and each one must be a column that other parts can refer to, such as totalAmount; the name is that column's key in the result, so a screen or a flow reads the total by name.
reasons.capabilityOperationError.description: Whoever handles a failed call, a person or an AI, needs to know when the error happens, for example a duplicate key because the row already exists; the sentence is shown with the contract, so error handling is written against a stated promise and not a guess.
reasons.conversionCaseWhen.equals: A case of a conversion matches when the old value equals a literal; the literal is the old code kept as written, so the step from old to new reads straight from the model with no code to interpret it.
reasons.field.defaultExpression: A new invoice should get its next number and today's date without the caller sending them; the expression runs on create when no value was supplied and is not applied on update, so defaults are decided in one place and an edit never overwrites a value.
reasons.flowStep.flow: A flow often reuses a smaller one, such as sending a receipt; the callFlow step names it, and the called flow runs under the caller's identity, trace and permission check, so reuse needs no copied steps.
reasons.httpConnector.baseUrlProperty: One customer account may talk to the outside service's sandbox while another talks to production; the property name points at a setting that, when it has a value for the calling tenant, overrides the fixed address, so the address changes in settings and not by editing the model.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.from: A transition is a move between two states; from names the state it leaves, so the engine refuses the move from any other state, for instance shipping an order that was never paid.
reasons.panelDataSource.onRowLoad: A table sometimes needs a computed column, such as remaining stock, that a plain query lacks; the named flow receives the loaded rows and adds fields to them, and the platform refuses a flow that changes the row count or the ids, so an enrichment cannot silently drop a row.
reasons.presentationMetadata.displayMode: A concept can carry a default display label into the screen metadata, such as standard, so a custom front end reads one declared choice from the model instead of keeping its own table of concept names; the built-in generated screens do not act on it today and use formPresentation, so this is a hint for hand-written front ends.
reasons.queryParameter.defaultExpression: A report of the last week should open without anyone typing dates; the expression, built from literals and a few registered functions such as addDays(today(), -7), fills the parameter when the caller sends none, so the default is declared beside the query it serves.
reasons.seed.alias: First-boot data often has rows that point at each other, such as an order line pointing at a seeded product; a record's alias is a local name that a later seed refers to with $ref:alias, so the author never copies a generated id.
